2.text: Manykin-Nevstruyev says that the Kolyma River was discovered in the

3.text: year 1638. Maydell mentions as the discoverer of the Kolyma the Cossack

4.text: Ivan Erastov, with his companions. He says that in 1644 three winter ham-

5.text: lets were founded on the Kolyma River, — Nishne-Kolymsk, Sredne-Kolymsk,

6.text: and Verkhne-Kolymsk (Lower Kolymsk, Middle Kolymsk, and Upper Kolymsk).¹

7.text: I am not sure that all three hamlets were founded as early as that, and all

8.text: in exactly the same year. On a copy of a chart of Siberia, made in the

9.text: year 1672 all three winter hamlets are mentioned, — the Lower, the Middle,

10.text: and the Upper. Nishne-Kolymsk in some documents was called “Dog Fortress,”

11.text: doubtless because of the dogs used for driving. It was the largest of the

12.text: three settlements. From Michael Stadukhin we have a report of the 22d of

13.text: April, 1647, taken down, as was the custom, from his own words, by the

14.text: Government clerk in the assembly-room (съѣзжая изба), in the presence of the

15.text: two governors of the Yakutsk Province, Pushkin and Suponev.² In this report

16.text: it is said that “the public-service official (служилый человѣкъ),³ Michael Stadukhin,

17.text: who, in the past 154th year (1646), went from the Kolyma River with the

18.text: Czar’s tribute, relates that he was on the Kolyma River two years for col-

19.text: lecting the Czar’s tribute. The Kolyma is a great river of the size of the

20.text: Lena. It runs in the same direction, east and north. On this Kolyma River

21.text: live the natives, Kolyma men of their own tribe, driving [Reindeer] and walking

22.text: [sedentary],⁴ — numerous people, — and they have a language of their own;

23.text: on this Kolyma, and also on a separate river, the Chiukhcha (чюхча), — and

24.text: this river Chiukhcha flows directly to the sea, and its mouth lies on this side

40.text: ² The Russian governors (воеводы) of the Moscow period were often sent in pairs, partly with the idea

41.text: that one would prevent any misdemeanor of the other.

42.text: ³ Thus were called all categories of soldiers and lower officials in the service of the Government.

43.text: ⁴ The Maritime (sedentary) Chukchee usually are called in the reports “walking,” in contrast to the

44.text: Reindeer division of the tribe. Among the Reindeer Chukchee each member of the family has a team of its

45.text: own: so all can drive. Among the Maritime Chukchee a family usually has but one team, and most of the

46.text: people have to walk. It seems that in earlier times the dog-teams of the Chukchee were still more unfit

47.text: for swift and efficient driving than they are now, in comparison with the dogs of the Maritime Koryak and

48.text: Russianized natives. So in a campaign the warriors of the Reindeer Chukchee were usually driving reindeer,

49.text: while the warriors of the Maritime Chukchee had to walk.
